wins.text: Record Q3 revenues of $22.1B, up 9% YoY, with every business posting record third-quarter revenue and positive operating leverage
Markets had a record Q3 with revenues up 15%; equities up 24% and fixed income up 12%, with prime balances up ~44%
Investment banking fees up 17% across all products: M&A +8%, ECM +35%, DCM +19%
Returned over $6B in capital to common shareholders in Q3, including $5B in share repurchases — $1B above guidance; $8.75B repurchased YTD under $20B program
USPB delivered record quarterly revenue of $5.3B with 12 consecutive quarters of positive operating leverage and ROTCE of 14.5%; Wealth posted record net new investment assets of $18.6B

risks.text: Goodwill impairment of $726M related to Banamex transaction reduced reported EPS to $1.86 vs. adjusted $2.24 and ROTCE to 8% vs. adjusted 9.7%

Full-year expenses guided higher than previously expected due to FX translation and revenue-linked compensation; efficiency ratio target of slightly below 64% (ex-impairment) implies Q4 expense step-up
Markets revenues expected to decline more than the historical 15%-20% sequential drop from Q3 to Q4, creating meaningful revenue headwind
Banamex deconsolidation will trigger ~$9B CTA flowing through P&L as a loss; regulatory approval for 25% stake sale expected to take 9-12 months, extending timeline uncertainty

Corporate nonaccrual loans increased materially quarter-over-quarter driven by 2 idiosyncratic downgrades; firm-wide ACL build of $2.5B cost of credit with unemployment scenario incorporating 7% downside rate

guidance_items.detail: Confident in exceeding $84B for full year 2025, up from prior $84B floor; NII ex-markets now expected up ~5.5% for full year vs. prior expectations
Full-year efficiency ratio expected slightly below 64% excluding goodwill impairment, consistent with prior guidance
Full-year expenses guided higher than previously expected due to FX and revenue-linked comp, pressuring near-term EPS
Markets Q4 sequential revenue decline expected to exceed historical 15%-20% range given exceptionally strong Q3
Credit cost expectations for the year unchanged; share repurchases to continue in Q4 under $20B program; CET1 target of ~12.8%

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: NBFI/non-depository financial institution loan exposure (~$104B) and credit quality within private credit and securitization portfolios
Stablecoin adoption strategy and competitive positioning vs. tokenized deposits for institutional payments
Sustainability of transformation expense base (~$3.5B) and ultimate end-state beyond 2026
